utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Would the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-02-65-I, the Prosecutor versus Zeljko Mejakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Nicholas Koumjian, Katharina Margetts, David Leese, and Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Koumjian. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Jovan Simic, attorney from Belgrade, and I'm representing Mr. Mejakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Simic. Mr. Mejakic, can you hear the proceeding in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And could you please answer the following questions for your identification: Would you please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zeljko Mejakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you please state your date and place of your birth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was born on the 2nd of August, 1964, in Petrov Gaj, Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And that's in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. This proceeding is an Initial Appearance of Mr. Zeljko Mejakic pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this International Tribunal. The original indictment against the accused was confirmed by a judge of this Tribunal more than eight years ago, that is, on the 13th of February, 1995. Subsequently thereafter, many developments in the original indictment arose until, in a decision dated 21st of November, 2002, the Trial Chamber III ordered the consolidated indictment against the accused and others, dated 5th of July, 2002, to be the operative indictment against the accused. Mr. Mejakic was transferred to this Tribunal on Friday last week, that is, 4th of July, 2003. Since this case has been already assigned to the Trial Chamber III, to which I belong, I'm presiding over this proceeding in the capacity as a member of it, though Judge Patrick Robinson has been assigned as the pre-trial Judge for this case. I shall now proceed to make certain that the accused understands the indictment against himself. Mr. Simic, has your client received the indictment in his own language?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, he has received the indictment in a language that he understands. He has read the indictment. He's understood the counts in the indictment. And our proposal is that we do not have to have the indictment read in full, but he can just plead according to the counts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then the next step will be the entry of a plea to the charges of the indictment. The accused may enter a plea within 30 days of the Initial Appearance, but he may enter a plea at the time of today, if he so wishes. So that is his intention, to plead today, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Mejakic, if you could rise and please plead to each count of the indictment which I'll put to you, confining yourself to either "guilty" or "not guilty." Count 1 of the indictment charges you with persecutions on political, racial, or religious grounds, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(h), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Count 2 of the indictment charges you with murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(a), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Count 3 of the indictment charges you with murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, which is punishable under Article 3, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Count 4 of the indictment charges you with inhumane acts, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(1), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And finally, count 5 of the indictment charges you with cruel treatment, violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Convention of 1949, punishable under Articles 3, 7(1), 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. You may sit down. I would like to ask the Registrar to note that Mr. Mejakic has pleaded not guilty to all five counts of the indictment. I must now remind the Prosecution that pursuant to Rule 66(A)(i), to make available within 30 days from now to the Defence, in a language which the accused understands, all the supporting materials which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought, also all prior statements obtained by the Prosecution from the accused must be disclosed as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We are ready to act on that, to begin acting on that today. However, what we have not yet prepared, is a general non-disclosure order, and I'm suggesting that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. perhaps the Court can today give us temporarily an oral order that the materials that we disclosed to counsel and to the accused not be disseminated to any other person other than the accused, his counsel, or appointed investigators, and that would include, of course, the current whereabouts and names of witnesses. If the Court would give that oral order, we can begin today or tomorrow providing the material to Defence counsel, and we are also preparing a general non-disclosure order with more specific requirements for Your Honour's signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Speaking for myself, I don't see any reason not to grant it. But if you have any observation from the Defence, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. I think that's a reasonable request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So the request was granted. Let me now turn to the Defence, and also tell the Defence that it will have a 30-day period for filing any preliminary motions that it may care to do once it has received all the supporting material in accordance with Rule 66(A)(i) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. And finally, pursuant to Rule 65 bis, a Status Conference shall be convened within 120 days of now, and further, pursuant to Rule 65 ter, the Senior Legal Officers assigned to Chambers may assist in performance of pre-trial functions entrusted to the Pre-Trial Judge, who is in this case Judge Patrick Robinson. In this regard, Ms. Yvonne Featherstone, the Senior Legal Officer of our Trial Chamber, shall undertake this task. Those being said, are there any matters the parties wish to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: A couple of matters, Your Honour. First, my understanding is that the spelling of Mr. Mejakic's last name is incorrect on the indictment. Perhaps we could ask him for the spelling, and including asking the interpreters to give the diacritics for his full name, first and last name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And what's the other thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And the other matter is a little more involved, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's handle the first matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mejakic, could you help me in this matter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, how do you spell your last name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] M-e-j-a-k-i-c with a vertical check above.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that is Mejakic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which is written as one of the nicknames.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's the third possibility that was given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down. That is solved, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, the other matter concerns Mr. Simic's representation. It's not our intent to interfere in choice of counsel, but it is our concern that the record be preserved for appeal that there not be issues on appeal. My understanding is that Mr. Simic also represents one of the accused on appeal from the Omarska case. That was a shift commander, Mr. Mejakic is accused of being a camp commander. There obviously is a potential for conflict of interest as to the responsibility, orders et cetera between the two. In fact, we have statements from the other accused that we believe are helpful against -- in our case against Mr. Mejakic. We suggest that the Court order the registrar -- my suggestion is the Court order the registrar to appoint an independent counsel to advise Mr. Mejakic as to the potential for a conflict, and assuming he waives that knowingly the record is preserved for appeal. But at the moment I believe there is an apparent conflict of interest and we need to do something to preserve the appeal record when counsel is representing two accused that could have a conflict of interest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. That matter is ultimately for the Registrar, I guess, but the -- oh, yes. Mr. Simic, do you have any observation?

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to inform you of the following, briefly. I'm not sure why my learned friend and colleague has not been informed, but I have been in touch with the Prosecutor, Carla Del Ponte. We've been reviewing this question and we reached a conclusion that we both share, namely, Mr. Brzakcin [phoen], Mr. Mejakic, both of the accused, when they are familiarised and informed about the possible conflict of interest, if they themselves fail to see this conflict of interest and provide written statements to both the Registry and the Office of the Prosecutor. We said that in that case, the Prosecution would not raise any further objections about this possible conflict of interest. We have provided both of these statements and we believe that conditions have been met, but we'll hear about this from the registry, eventually. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll just say that I was just assigned to this case and it is very possible that there are other matters that I was not informed about. I thank Mr. Simic regarding that. Finally, the only other issue I wanted to raise is my understanding, Your Honour, is that there is a date set for hearing for the other accused. Would it make sense to set Mr. Mejakic's hearing, 65 ter, for the same date?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My understanding is that the 65 ter conference is scheduled for next week, or a week after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think the 65 ter conference is scheduled at the week of 22, with the other accused, and Mr. Simic is invited to participate in that 65 ter conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. We shall be present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then unless there is anything to be raised, the proceeding is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: adjourned at 3.20 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: [Trial Chamber and Senior Legal Officer confer]
